headline: Anti-monopoly penalty tips Trip.com into a GAAP loss
summary_short: Trip.com Group's Q2 2026 net revenue rose 6% y/y to RMB15.7 billion, but a RMB5.18 billion SAMR anti-monopoly penalty drove a GAAP net loss of RMB2.46 billion versus a RMB4.85 billion profit a year earlier.
summary_long: Total net revenue grew 6% y/y to RMB15.7bn (US$2.3bn) but fell 3% q/q on elevated energy prices, geopolitical volatility, and operational adjustments. Accommodation revenue rose 6% y/y to RMB6.6bn despite a SAMR contra-revenue charge; transportation ticketing fell 1% y/y and 12% q/q on macro headwinds; packaged-tour and corporate travel both grew double digits. A RMB5.18bn SAMR anti-monopoly penalty pushed operating income and net income attributable to shareholders into losses of RMB1.46bn and RMB2.46bn, versus RMB4.85bn profit a year earlier. Non-GAAP diluted EPS rose to RMB7.27 from RMB7.20; adjusted EBITDA margin compressed to 29% from 33%. Cash and investments stood at RMB100.5bn at quarter-end.
confidence_notes: Values are RMB with USD conversion per the release's stated rate (USD1.00=RMB6.7851 as of June 30, 2026). The shard's own ebit_usd_m/ebitda_usd_m KPIs (both -2099, unit CNY) don't match the release's reported operating loss (RMB1,462M) or its Adjusted EBITDA (RMB4,565M, positive) — likely a different Yahoo-derived proxy; the release's own reconciliation table was used instead. Q2 2026 results include a one-off RMB5,180M (US$763M) anti-monopoly penalty from China's SAMR that drove operating and net income into losses; excluding it, management states net income would have been RMB2.7bn.

drivers.explanation: Decline attributed to macro headwinds — elevated energy prices and geopolitical volatility — versus both the prior quarter and prior year.
Growth driven by an increase in accommodation reservations, partially offset by a contra-revenue charge imposed by China's SAMR.
Swing to an operating loss driven by a RMB5,180M anti-monopoly penalty from SAMR; ex-penalty, G&A would have risen only 5% y/y.
Company attributes the GAAP net loss to the one-off SAMR anti-monopoly penalty; underlying profitability and international growth (platform revenue +50% y/y) held up.
